item.title: TT-104: Undo for TaskStore add/complete/delete
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (contains the tasktracker package and BACKLOG.md). Implement ticket TT-104 from BACKLOG.md exactly as written:

`tasktracker.store.TaskStore` has `add`, `complete` and `delete`. Add `undo()`:
- It reverts the most recent not-yet-undone `add`, `complete` or `delete`; repeated calls walk further back (LIFO), across all three kinds.
- Undoing an `add` removes that task; undoing a `complete` makes the task open again; undoing a `delete` restores the task exactly as it was, under the same id.
- Ids are never reused, even after undoing an `add`.
- With nothing left to undo, `undo()` raises `NothingToUndo` (defined in `tasktracker.store`).
- Failed operations (e.g. completing an unknown id) are not recorded.

Acceptance: existing tests keep passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; add unit tests covering each rule above, including a mixed LIFO sequence, undo of a delete restoring the same id and state, id non-reuse after undoing an add, and failed operations not being recorded; standard library only. Keep changes minimal, functions under 60 lines, and avoid unnecessary comments. Commit only this ticket, as one commit, with the repository's configured git identity and no tool attribution lines. Do not push. Stay in your workspace. Do not ask the operator questions; if something is ambiguous, pick the most reasonable reading and state it in your summary.

item.title: TT-103: Search query syntax in search()
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (contains the tasktracker package and BACKLOG.md). Implement ticket TT-103 from BACKLOG.md exactly as written:

`tasktracker.search.search(tasks, query)` only does a case-sensitive substring match on titles. Support a small query language instead:
- The query is split into terms on whitespace, except inside double quotes: `"fix login"` is one phrase term. All terms must match (AND).
- A bare word or phrase matches when it appears in the title, case-insensitively.
- `tag:NAME` matches tasks that have the tag NAME (exact tag, case-insensitive).
- `status:open` / `status:done` match on status.
- Any other `field:value` term, an unknown status, or an unterminated quote raises `QueryError` (defined in `tasktracker.search`).
- An empty or blank query matches every task. Results keep the input order.

Acceptance: existing tests keep passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; add unit tests for every rule above; standard library only. Keep changes minimal, functions under 60 lines, and avoid unnecessary comments. Commit only this ticket, as one commit, with the repository's configured git identity and no tool attribution lines. Do not push. Stay in your workspace. Do not ask the operator questions; if something is ambiguous, pick the most reasonable reading and state it in your summary.

item.title: TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export in to_csv
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (contains the tasktracker package and BACKLOG.md). Implement ticket TT-102 from BACKLOG.md exactly as written:

`tasktracker.export.to_csv(tasks)` joins fields with commas and breaks on titles containing commas, quotes or newlines. It must produce RFC 4180 CSV:
- Header `id,title,tags,status,due`; one row per task in the given order.
- Tags joined with `;`, due date as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` or empty.
- A field containing a comma, double quote, CR or LF is wrapped in double quotes, with embedded double quotes doubled. Other fields are not quoted.
- Every line (header included) ends with CRLF.

Acceptance: existing tests keep passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; add unit tests for each rule above (including titles with commas, quotes, CR and LF, and an empty tag list/empty due date); standard library only. Keep changes minimal, functions under 60 lines, and avoid unnecessary comments. Commit only this ticket, as one commit, with the repository's configured git identity and no tool attribution lines. Do not push. Stay in your workspace. Do not ask the operator questions; if something is ambiguous, pick the most reasonable reading and state it in your summary.

item.title: TT-101: Reject impossible due dates in parse_due
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (contains the tasktracker package and BACKLOG.md). Implement ticket TT-101 from BACKLOG.md exactly as written:

`tasktracker.dates.parse_due(text, today)` silently clamps impossible dates: `2026-02-30` becomes `2026-02-28`. Instead:
- An impossible calendar date (`2026-02-30`, `2025-02-29`, `2026-04-31`, `2026-13-01`, `2026-00-10`) raises `InvalidDate`, a `ValueError` subclass defined in `tasktracker.dates`, whose message contains the original text.
- Anything else that does not match a supported form also raises `InvalidDate` (today it raises a bare `ValueError`).
- Relative offsets: `+Nd` is N days after `today`, `+0d` is `today`. Negative or unsigned offsets (`-3d`, `3d`) raise `InvalidDate`.
- `today` and `tomorrow` keep working; matching stays case-insensitive and ignores surrounding whitespace.

Acceptance: existing tests keep passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; add unit tests for every case above; standard library only. Keep changes minimal, functions under 60 lines, and avoid unnecessary comments. Commit only this ticket, as one commit, with the repository's configured git identity and no tool attribution lines. Do not push. Stay in your workspace. Do not ask the operator questions; if something is ambiguous, pick the most reasonable reading and state it in your summary.

pr.body: Approach: InvalidDate(ValueError) in tasktracker/dates.py. parse_due validates calendar dates instead of clamping, rejects unsupported forms and signed or unsigned offsets outside +Nd/+0d, and keeps today, tomorrow, case-insensitive matching and whitespace trimming. Key files: tasktracker/dates.py, tests/test_dates.py (new, 14 tests in the suite). Checks: unittest discover, 14 tests OK on tree 8b5cd8fd4800e0abecaac1c2b24342f56ff5e3a2. Review: whole-change reviewer agt_01M7W5Z1Y8T6KA8AYKEBBTX0AH passed head 2f8979f with no blocking findings. Follow-ups, non-blocking: bare OverflowError for tomorrow at date.max; bare ValueError from int() for very long digit offsets; neither edge is tested; no boundary asserts. Assumptions: callers catching ValueError keep working since InvalidDate subclasses it. parse_due has no other callers in the repo besides tests/test_basic.py, which passes.
pr.summary: parse_due no longer clamps impossible dates. Now raises InvalidDate for impossible dates, unsupported text and negative or unsigned offsets. Before: 2026-02-30 became 2026-02-28 and -3d/3d raised bare ValueError. Now: InvalidDate with the original text in the message.
pr.title: TT-101: reject impossible due dates in parse_due

risk.why: parse_due's behaviour changes for invalid input: it now raises InvalidDate instead of clamping or a bare ValueError. The change is contained behind the existing parse_due interface. InvalidDate subclasses ValueError. The only in-repo caller, tests/test_basic.py, passes. The reviewer confirmed medium.
